description: Clips the signal at clip_level and writes a NOISE pattern of depth 'depth' onto the clipped stretches (submode 1; submode 2 imposes a pitched waveform instead - separate entry). Duration static and SAMPLE-EXACT on all probes. Although the clipped-region fill is 'noise', the program never seeds its generator, so every run is byte-identical (deterministic by construction, same as distort reform). Output is rescaled: peak lands at clip_level/(1+clip_level) (0.2308 at 0.3, 0.1667 at 0.2 - observed). depth IS breakpoint-capable (verified against both endpoints); clip_level's breakpoint path is BROKEN on this build (see known_issues) - keep clip_level scalar. Works on any material including unipolar (no waveset dependence). MONO only.
musical_use: Fuzz-with-texture: everything above the clip ceiling becomes noise-crusted distortion while quieter material passes clean, so the effect dynamically keys itself to the source's loud moments. Low clip_level (0.1-0.3) crushes most of the signal into roaring grit; higher levels only singe the peaks. depth sets how audible the noise fill is - near 0 a hard clipper, near 1 a sandpaper roar. Breakpoint depth to morph from clean clipping into noisy destruction across the file. For a pitched buzz instead of noise on the clipped stretches use submode 2.

clip_level.description: Clipping ceiling, 0-1 (CDP-enforced; 1.5 refused verbatim). 0 is accepted but renders DIGITAL SILENCE (peak 0.0000 - avoid). Output peak scales to about clip_level/(1+clip_level). SCALAR ONLY despite the banner's 'may vary over time': the breakpoint path is broken (see known_issues).

depth.description: Depth of the noise pattern written onto clipped stretches, 0-1 (1.5 refused verbatim). Breakpoint-capable, banner-confirmed and verified (0.1->1.0 ramp differs from both endpoint renders; a near-constant brk also behaves sanely).

examples.description: Self-keying fuzz on the loud moments only.
examples.expected_use: Peaks crush into noisy grit, quiet passages stay clean; same length, peak ~0.29.
Starts as hard clipping, ends as full noise-crust distortion.

known_issues: CLIP_LEVEL BREAKPOINT BROKEN (first-class): a breakpoint file in the clip_level slot exits 0 but collapses the output to a fixed near-silent buzz (peak 0.0099, uniform RMS 0.0075) REGARDLESS of the values - a 0.2->0.8 ramp and a 0.3->0.30001 near-constant ramp render byte-identical to each other and unlike any scalar render. Entry pins clip_level scalar-only.
clip_level 0 is accepted and renders digital silence (88200 frames, peak 0.0000) - the engine's silence check will flag it; not a crash.
The 'noise' fill is deterministic: unseeded generator, repeat runs byte-identical 1.2 s apart. No way to get a different noise pattern.
Unipolar / zero-crossing-free material ACCEPTED (level-domain process, no waveset dependence) - full-length output verified.
Stereo refused: 'Application doesn't work with this type of infile.' (exit 255) -> mono.
